metadata.description: Per-country search-targeting profiles for MOSAIC AI cholera data collection
metadata.notes: health_domains are candidate URLs and are NOT verified by this builder. Run py/verify_country_profiles.py to URL-check them and write reference/country_profiles_domain_status.json. neighbors may include non-MOSAIC countries for regional-context queries only - data collection remains restricted to the 40 MOSAIC framework countries plus named pilot countries (reference/pipeline_countries.json).

AGO.name: Angola
AGO.season: Rainy season Oct-Apr; Luanda peri-urban outbreaks; 2006 and 2025 major epidemics

BDI.name: Burundi
BDI.season: Lake Tanganyika shoreline endemic focus; rainy seasons Feb-May and Sep-Dec

BEN.name: Benin
BEN.season: Coastal lagoon foci (Cotonou, Oueme delta, So-Ava, Abomey-Calavi); primary rains Apr-Jul, but outbreaks cluster in the Aug-Nov secondary window

BFA.name: Burkina Faso
BFA.season: Rainy season Jun-Sep; displacement-linked risk in Sahel and Centre-Nord

BGD.name: Bangladesh

pre_1971: East Pakistan (WHO reported 'Pakistan' as one country)

disease_terms: ডায়রিয়া (diarrhoea: context only, never counted as cholera)
acute watery diarrhoea (AWD: not cholera unless the source says cholera)
BGD.season: Hyperendemic, bimodal: pre-monsoon peak Mar-May and post-monsoon peak Sep-Dec. Flood-associated surges 1988, 1998, 2004, 2007, 2022 (Sylhet), 2024 (Feni). O139 Bengal emerged 1992-93. Rohingya camps in Cox's Bazar since Aug 2017 (~0.9-1 M people)
regional_sources: WHO SEARO (searo.who.int) and WHO Bangladesh country office (who.int/bangladesh)
WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record annual cholera reports incl. 2025 (iris.who.int, cdn.who.int) - Table 3 gives tested/positive; read the case definition each year
WHO Cox's Bazar EWARS weekly bulletins and ISCG situation reports (cdn.who.int, rohingyaresponse.org) - camp data, sub-national only
WHO multi-country cholera situation reports / epidemiological updates
icddr,b Health and Science Bulletin, Glimpse, annual reports (icddrb.org, dspace.icddrb.org); Journal of Health, Population and Nutrition (JHPN)
IEDCR outbreak investigation reports and the National Cholera Control Plan 2019-2030 (iedcr.gov.bd, dghs.gov.bd)
DGHS Health Bulletins (annual) and emergency-operations daily reports
IFRC GO / DREF operations (go.ifrc.org); ReliefWeb - use py/reliefweb.py
archive_hints: Cholera Research Laboratory (Dacca) annual reports and Matlab trial reports, 1960-1978 (dspace.icddrb.org)
icddr,b library and DSpace repository; Bangladesh Medical Research Council Bulletin
WHO SEARO archives and WHO IRIS (WER 1970-2000 cholera tables)
The Daily Star and Prothom Alo archives
Wayback Machine for old.dghs.gov.bd and iedcr.gov.bd (refused connections or need a login in testing)
country_notes: PILOT COUNTRY (Bangladesh, BGD). Outside the 40 MOSAIC countries; processed only because it was named. These rules override the general ones where they differ. Plan: docs/technical/bangladesh-pilot-plan.md.

WHAT MATTERS: Bangladesh has almost no national count of suspected cholera. Most of its numbers are diarrhoea, sentinel samples or camp counts. The goal is to record what each number counts, not to maximise coverage. A wrong national number is worse than none.

FIVE STREAMS - classify every figure before entering it: (1) NATIONAL NOTIFICATIONS to WHO (WER annual tables; 1971-2000 small and very incomplete); (2) SENTINEL SURVEILLANCE (icddr,b 2% systematic sample at Dhaka hospital, Matlab, the IEDCR/icddr,b national cholera surveillance at ~22 hospitals from 2014, later 20 suspected cases sampled per site per week) - WHO's annual totals since 2023 (23,369 / 24,758 / 22,709) come from this stream: diarrhoea patients enrolled, not national cholera; (3) COX'S BAZAR CAMPS (WHO/ISCG EWARS; the WHO dashboard row 'Bangladesh' is the camps only); (4) DIARRHOEA/AWD totals (DGHS, IEDCR, flood reports) - NOT cholera; (5) BURDEN ESTIMATES (e.g. ~110,000 a year, Ali et al. 2015) - model output, never an observation. Also: DGHS DHIS2 / Health Bulletin counts coded 'cholera' (ICD-10 A00) are a clinical label (count type mixed), and O139 was reported separately in 1992-93.

LOCATIONS: SEAR::BGD (national), SEAR::BGD::<Division>[::<District>]. AFR:: is rejected. py/add_observation.py writes the [BGD-PILOT] tag for you; py/validate_quality.py errors on any AI row without it. Cox's Bazar camps: SEAR::BGD::Chattogram::Cox's Bazar (JHU's 'Chittagong Division::Cox's Bazar' and 'Chattogram::BD-11' are the same place; JHU 21127 at BD-11 is camp AWD, not cholera). Matlab is in Chandpur district: SEAR::BGD::Chattogram::Chandpur (JHU uses BD-09). icddr,b Dhaka hospital: SEAR::BGD::Dhaka::Dhaka.

NEVER AT SEAR::BGD: camp counts, sentinel-site counts, one-hospital counts. Put them at the site's own location. If a source gives only a national total from sentinel sites, enter it at SEAR::BGD and say 'sentinel' in processing_notes; Agent 7 records its coverage. Never scale a sample count up to a national figure.

CASE DEFINITIONS: sCh = suspected cholera as the source defines it; cCh = culture-, PCR- or RDT-positive cholera (say which in processing_notes). NEVER put diarrhoea, AWD or AGE totals in sCh or cCh unless the source itself calls them cholera. Quote the source's case definition for every national figure.

SENTINEL POSITIVITY: tested/positive counts by site go in ./data/BGD/sentinel_positivity_ai.csv (columns: Location, TL, TR, site, tested, positive, test_method, serogroup, sampling, source_index, source, processing_notes), not in cholera_data_ai.csv. Register the source first with py/add_observation.py register-source. Write with Python's csv module; never hand-edit. The validator checks it. Matlab (population-based) first.

COUNT TYPES: ./reference/count_basis/BGD.csv records what every national source-year counts and its coverage (national / subset / sample). strict_basis is on: the weekly builder uses NO national value, AI rows included, until it has an entry there. Agent 7 adds an AI:<metadata Index> entry with a quoted case definition for every national AI row with a count. Read the table before searching: at set-up every national source-year is held out.
NO ZERO ROWS: Bangladesh is hyperendemic. add-zero and sCh=0 are refused. Do not record absence anywhere.

AGENT 3 IS REPURPOSED: do not validate zero transmission. Map the surveillance system year by year 1970-2025: which streams existed (WHO notification, icddr,b 2% surveillance, Matlab HDSS, national cholera surveillance 2014-, IEDCR AWD/EWARS, Cox's Bazar EWARS from 2017, DHIS2), their case definitions, sentinel site lists, sampling fractions and test methods. Agent 3 writes no rows to cholera_data_ai.csv; its search log is the evidence for Agent 7's count-basis entries.
GAP FILES: Bangladesh's gap files are in ./reference/pilot/, not the shared 40-country files. Coverage % there counts any row and is not a measure of success.

SOURCES: ./reference/priority_sources_pilot.txt lists Bangladesh's pre-authorized domains (in addition to ./reference/priority_sources.txt). Use the profile's regional_sources in place of WHO AFRO / Africa CDC and archive_hints in place of francophone/lusophone archives. ReliefWeb via py/reliefweb.py (may need SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem).

PRIORITIES: (1) what JHU 429's 2018-2022 national figures count (566 / 503 / 212 / 477 / 1,191; probably sentinel laboratory positives); (2) the WER case definition for each year with a national figure, 1971-2000 and 2023-2025 (Table 3 tested/positive, age split); (3) any national suspected cholera count for 2001-2022 (DGHS Health Bulletins, IEDCR); (4) sentinel positivity series, Matlab first; (5) Cox's Bazar weekly series 2017-2026 at sub-national level. Do not spend the query budget on single-hospital clinical studies.

AGENT 7 TRIPWIRES: retype any year typed national suspected where the source shows an under-5 share above 30% or tested / cases above 50% (signatures of sentinel or diarrhoea data); flag any national suspected year below 1% of the ~110,000 burden estimate as incomplete. search_report.txt must include a 1970-2025 table: stream(s) present, what each counts, with quoted source text.

BWA.name: Botswana
BWA.season: Rare; importation risk via Zimbabwe/Zambia borders (Chobe, North East)

CAF.name: Central African Republic
CAF.season: Ubangi river corridor (Bangui, Mobaye, Basse-Kotto); conflict-disrupted surveillance

CIV.name: Cote d'Ivoire
CIV.season: Abidjan lagoon precarious settlements; rainy season May-Jul

CMR.name: Cameroon
CMR.season: South-West (Bakassi peninsula, Ekondo Titi, Bamusso) and Littoral/Douala dominated the 2021-23 epidemic, the largest recent event - Far North had almost no cases in it. Far North (Logone/Chari, Lake Chad basin) is the HISTORICAL pre-2020 focus. Dual French/English reporting.

COD.name: Democratic Republic of Congo
COD.season: Endemic Great Lakes foci (Sud-Kivu/Uvira, Nord-Kivu, Tanganyika); epidemic spread along Congo river to Kinshasa

COG.name: Republic of the Congo
COG.season: Congo/Ubangi river corridor; cross-border with Kinshasa

ERI.name: Eritrea
ERI.season: Minimal public reporting; treat absence of data as non-reporting unless positively documented

ETH.name: Ethiopia
ETH.season: Reported historically as 'AWD' rather than cholera - search both terms; Oromia/Somali/Amhara foci

GHA.name: Ghana
GHA.season: Greater Accra urban epidemics; rainy season Apr-Jul; 2014 major epidemic

GIN.name: Guinea
GIN.season: Coastal Conakry/Boke foci; rainy season Jun-Oct

GMB.name: Gambia
GMB.season: Rare; Gambia river corridor; shares epidemiology with Senegal

GNB.name: Guinea-Bissau
GNB.season: Bissau urban epidemics; rainy season Jun-Oct; 1994/2005/2008 major epidemics

KEN.name: Kenya
KEN.season: Refugee camps (Dadaab, Kakuma), Nairobi informal settlements, lake and coastal counties; rains Mar-May, Oct-Dec

LBR.name: Liberia
LBR.season: Monrovia (West Point, Clara Town) urban foci; rainy season May-Oct

MLI.name: Mali
MLI.season: Niger river corridor (Mopti, Tombouctou, Gao); rainy season Jul-Sep; conflict-disrupted surveillance in north

MOZ.name: Mozambique
MOZ.season: Cyclone/flood-driven epidemics (Idai 2019, Freddy 2023); rainy season Nov-Apr; DNSP publishes cholera bulletins

MRT.name: Mauritania
MRT.season: Senegal river valley (Trarza, Gorgol, Brakna); shares epidemiology with Senegal/Mali

MWI.name: Malawi
MWI.season: Lake Malawi shoreline and Shire valley (Nsanje, Chikwawa, Karonga); rainy season Nov-Apr, but the 2022-23 epidemic (largest recorded) persisted through the dry season - a strict seasonal filter will under-search it

NAM.name: Namibia
NAM.season: Northern regions bordering Angola (Kunene, Omusati, Ohangwena); flood-linked

NER.name: Niger
NER.season: Niger river valley and Nigeria border (Maradi, Zinder, Dosso, Tahoua); rainy season Jun-Sep

NGA.name: Nigeria
NGA.season: NCDC publishes weekly cholera sitreps; north-east conflict states (Borno, Yobe, Adamawa) and Lagos; rainy season Jun-Oct

NPL.name: Nepal
disease_terms: झाडापखाला (diarrhoea/AGE: context only, never counted as cholera)
acute gastroenteritis (AGE: context only, never counted as cholera)
NPL.season: Monsoon Jun-Sep; Kathmandu Valley urban outbreaks (2016, 2022, 2024); Terai (Madhesh, Lumbini: Kapilvastu 2021, Birgunj 2025) and far-west hill outbreaks; 1990-91 major epidemic (WHO annual 23,888 and 30,648)
regional_sources: WHO SEARO (searo.who.int) and WHO Nepal country office (who.int/nepal)
WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record annual cholera reports (iris.who.int)
WHO multi-country cholera situation reports / epidemiological updates
EDCD EWARS weekly bulletins and outbreak situation reports (edcd.gov.np; mirrored on ReliefWeb - use py/reliefweb.py)
DoHS annual reports (dohs.gov.np; indexed by Nepali fiscal year)
Nepal Health Research Council journals (jnhrc.com.np, elibrary.nhrc.gov.np)

Wayback Machine for edcd.gov.np and dohs.gov.np (both refused connections in testing)
country_notes: PILOT COUNTRY (Nepal, NPL). Outside the 40 MOSAIC countries; processed only because it was named. These rules override the general ones where they differ.

LOCATIONS: use SEAR::NPL (national), SEAR::NPL::<Province>[::<District>]. AFR:: is rejected for Nepal. py/add_observation.py writes the [NPL-PILOT] tag into processing_notes for you; py/validate_quality.py errors on any AI row without it.
GAP FILES: Nepal's gap files are in ./reference/pilot/ (same file names as ./reference/effective_surveillance_*.csv), not in the shared 40-country files.

CASE DEFINITIONS: suspected/AWD outbreak totals go in sCh; culture- or RDT-confirmed counts go in cCh. NEVER put acute gastroenteritis (AGE, झाडापखाला) or general diarrhoea totals in sCh or cCh: Nepal reports AGE (about 7-8k cases a year at sentinel sites) separately from cholera.

WHO/WER ANNUAL FIGURES: quote the case definition the source used. Some WHO annual totals for Nepal are confirmed-only (2016: 169 = the confirmed count; 2023: 7; 2024: 95). If a WHO/WER figure is confirmed-only, enter it as cCh, not sCh.
EWARS: EWARS weekly counts come from sentinel hospitals (40 in 2015, 118 in 2022) and are lab-confirmed. Record them as cCh at SEAR::NPL and say 'sentinel hospitals' in processing_notes.

NO ZERO ROWS: do not add zero rows for Nepal (add-zero and sCh=0 are refused). Record years or weeks with no cases reported, and sentinel zero weeks, in ./data/NPL/cholera_presence_ai.csv or your search log instead. Agent 3 (zero-transmission) documents absence evidence in its log only.

BIKRAM SAMBAT DATES: convert every BS date and fiscal year to Gregorian (fiscal year 20XX/YY starts on Shrawan 1, about mid-July; e.g. FY 2077/78 = mid-Jul 2020 to mid-Jul 2021) and quote the original in processing_notes.

COUNT TYPES: the weekly builder uses only rows whose count type is recorded in ./reference/count_basis/NPL.csv. Read it before searching; many entries are 'provisional' or 'unknown'. Agent 7 adds an entry (source_key AI:<metadata Index>) for any AI source that reports WHO/WER annual figures, with a quote as evidence, and upgrades 'provisional' entries it can verify.

HELD-OUT YEARS: the gap files count every row as coverage, but these years have NO usable national suspected count as of 2026-11-20 (see ./data/NPL/builder_holdout.csv and ./data/NPL/cholera_period_totals_NPL.csv): 2007-2009, 2011-2015, 2017-2020 (plus the true gap 1999-2006). The 2011-2014 JHU figures (collection 21301) look like AGE; 2012, 2016 and 2023-2024 WHO annual figures are confirmed-only. Treat these years as gaps for suspected cases.

SOURCES: ./reference/priority_sources_pilot.txt lists Nepal's pre-authorized domains (in addition to ./reference/priority_sources.txt). Use the profile's regional_sources in place of WHO AFRO / Africa CDC and archive_hints in place of francophone/lusophone archives.
UNREACHABLE SITES: edcd.gov.np and dohs.gov.np refused connections in testing. Use the Wayback Machine and ReliefWeb (py/reliefweb.py; may need SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/cert.pem).

PRIORITIES: (1) a documented count type for every source-year 2018-2025; (2) the 2021 conflict: 2,023 (Kapilvastu, JHU 21541) vs WHO annual 1,609; (3) the 2024 conflict: WHO dashboard 360 vs 95 confirmed; (4) suspected totals for the EWARS years 2020-2022; (5) gaps 1999-2006 (Agents 1 and 4) and 1982-88 (Agent 4: NHRC eLibrary, Gorkhapatra, WHO SEARO archives).

RWA.name: Rwanda
RWA.season: Lake Kivu shoreline (Rubavu, Rusizi) with DRC cross-border importation

SEN.name: Senegal
SEN.season: Touba Magal mass gathering historically amplified epidemics; rainy season Jul-Oct

SLE.name: Sierra Leone
SLE.season: Freetown coastal slums; rainy season May-Oct; 2012 major epidemic

SOM.name: Somalia
SOM.season: Endemic; Shabelle/Juba riverine districts and IDP camps; drought and flood cycles; reported as AWD/cholera jointly

SSD.name: South Sudan
SSD.season: Nile corridor, PoC/IDP sites, Renk transit centres; 2024-25 epidemic; conflict-disrupted surveillance

SWZ.name: Eswatini
SWZ.season: Rare; importation risk from Mozambique and South Africa

TCD.name: Chad
TCD.season: Lake Chad basin and Sudan border refugee influx (Ouaddai, Sila); 2025 epidemic linked to Sudan crisis; rainy season Jun-Sep

TGO.name: Togo
TGO.season: Lome coastal/lagoon foci in Maritime region; rainy season Apr-Jul

TZA.name: Tanzania
TZA.season: Lake Victoria and Tanganyika basins, Dar es Salaam, Zanzibar; rains Mar-May and Oct-Dec

UGA.name: Uganda
UGA.season: Lake Albert/Edward fishing communities, Karamoja, refugee settlements (Bidibidi, Adjumani); rains Mar-May, Sep-Nov

ZAF.name: South Africa
ZAF.season: NICD publishes outbreak reports; 2000-01 KZN epidemic, 2023 Hammanskraal outbreak; mostly imported cases otherwise

ZMB.name: Zambia
ZMB.season: Lusaka peri-urban (Kanyama, Chawama) and Lake Mweru/Tanganyika fishing camps; rainy season Nov-Apr; 2023-24 major epidemic

ZWE.name: Zimbabwe
ZWE.season: 2008-09 epidemic (~98k cases) is the reference event; Harare (Budiriro, Glen View) and Manicaland; rainy season Nov-Mar
